questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of the following pairs of personality and the associated musical instrument is NOT matched correctly?
questions.explanation_en: Pandit Bhajan Sopori was a renowned santoor maestro from Kashmir, not a veena player, so pair 3 is wrongly matched. The others are correct: Zakir Hussain – tabla, Ustad Bismillah Khan – shehnai, Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia – bansuri (flute).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which Constitutional Amendment Act promoted the appointment of the same person as a Governor for two or more states?
questions.explanation_en: The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 — enacted alongside the States Reorganisation Act — amended Article 153 to allow the same person to be appointed Governor of two or more states. It also reorganised states on a linguistic basis and abolished the Part A/B/C/D classification.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Where is the India's first Dark Night Sky Reserve being established?
questions.explanation_en: India's first Dark Sky Reserve is being set up at Hanle in Ladakh, within the Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, around the Indian Astronomical Observatory. It was announced in 2022 by the UT administration with the Indian Institute of Astrophysics to promote astro-tourism and protect the night sky from light pollution.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of the following types of structures is NOT associated with Buddhist architecture in India?
questions.explanation_en: Buddhist architecture in India consists of stupas (relic mounds), chaityas (prayer halls with a stupa at one end) and viharas (monasteries where monks lived). 'Monkas' is not a Buddhist structure — it is simply a distractor word — so it is the correct choice.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: The first Indian to participate in NASA's International Air and Space Program was _____.
questions.explanation_en: Jahnavi Dangeti, a student from Andhra Pradesh, became the first Indian to complete NASA's International Air and Space Program (IASP) in 2022, held at the Kennedy Space Center, USA. The other names are not associated with this programme.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which of the following was the host country for the FIFA World Cup 2022?
questions.explanation_en: The FIFA World Cup 2022 was hosted by Qatar (20 November – 18 December 2022), the first World Cup held in the Middle East and the first played in November–December. Argentina won the final against France on penalties.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which of the following states has the highest number of operating mines (excluding fuels, atomic mineral and minor minerals), according to the Annual Report, 2021-22 of the Ministry of Mines?
questions.explanation_en: According to the Ministry of Mines Annual Report 2021-22, Madhya Pradesh had the highest number of reporting (operating) mines in the country, followed by Gujarat, Karnataka and Odisha. Odisha leads in the value of mineral production, but by number of mines Madhya Pradesh is first.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: As of December 2022, who was the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi?
questions.explanation_en: Vinai Kumar Saxena took over as the 22nd Lieutenant Governor of Delhi on 26 May 2022, succeeding Anil Baijal, and was therefore the LG in December 2022. Najeeb Jung and Tajendra Khanna were earlier LGs of Delhi.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a sexually transmitted disease?
questions.explanation_en: Amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery) is caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica and spreads through contaminated food and water, not by sexual contact. AIDS (HIV), gonorrhoea and syphilis are all sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between the forces of Rana Sanga and _____.
questions.explanation_en: The Battle of Khanwa (17 March 1527) was fought near Fatehpur Sikri between Babur and the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga of Mewar. Babur's victory, following Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi, consolidated Mughal rule in north India.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which of the following eras is considered as the age of the dinosaurs?
questions.explanation_en: The Mesozoic Era (about 252 to 66 million years ago, comprising the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods) is called the 'Age of Reptiles' or age of the dinosaurs. The Cenozoic that followed is the age of mammals, while the Palaeozoic preceded the dinosaurs.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: 'Buiya' is a popular folk-dance form of which of the following states?
questions.explanation_en: Buiya is a folk dance of the Digaru Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, performed on festive occasions. Other Arunachal dances include Ponung, Wancho and Bardo Chham.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: What name was given to the operation for liberation of Goa, in 1961, to make it a part of the Union of India?
questions.explanation_en: Operation Vijay (December 1961) was the Indian armed forces' action that liberated Goa, Daman and Diu from Portuguese rule. Operation Polo (1948) was the annexation of Hyderabad, and Operation Searchlight (1971) was a Pakistani army action in East Pakistan.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD), in partnership with the Ministry of Education, GOI and UNICEF, launched which of the following campaigns to bring back 'out of school' adolescent girls in India to the formal education and/or skilling system?
questions.explanation_en: Kanya Shiksha Pravesh Utsav was launched in March 2022 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development with the Ministry of Education and UNICEF, to bring out-of-school adolescent girls (11–14 years) back into formal education or skilling, using the Anganwadi network under Mission Shakti.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: National Action Plan for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) is a joint initiative of _____ and _____.

options.en: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment and Climate Change; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment and Climate Change; Ministry of Minority Affairs
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Ministry of Environment and Climate Change

questions.explanation_en: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem), launched in 2022, is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. It aims to end hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by promoting mechanised sanitation and skilling sanitation workers.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: How many internal reflections do light rays undergo, inside a raindrop, to form a secondary rainbow?
questions.explanation_en: A primary rainbow forms by one internal reflection inside each raindrop, while a secondary rainbow forms by two internal reflections. The extra reflection makes the secondary bow fainter, larger and with its colour order reversed.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: As per the Census of India 2011, what percentage of Indians live in rural areas?
questions.explanation_en: As per Census 2011, about 68.8% of India's population (83.3 crore people) lived in rural areas and 31.2% in urban areas. The urban share rose from 27.8% in 2001, showing gradual urbanisation.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: The formula for calculating Net National Product (NNP) is _____.
questions.explanation_en: Net National Product (NNP) = Gross National Product (GNP) − Depreciation. Depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) is the wear and tear of capital goods; subtracting it from GNP gives the net value of output produced by a country's residents.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which of the following states had the highest growth rate for population according to the Census of India, 2011 as compared to that of 2001?
questions.explanation_en: According to Census 2011, Meghalaya recorded the highest decadal population growth rate among the given states, about 27.9% during 2001–2011 (Bihar ~25.4%, UP ~20.2%, Himachal ~12.9%). Nagaland was the only state to record negative growth in that decade.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Who among the following was the first woman president of the Indian Olympic Association?
questions.explanation_en: Legendary sprinter P.T. Usha became the first woman president of the Indian Olympic Association, elected unopposed in December 2022. Known as the 'Payyoli Express', she finished fourth in the 400 m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which ministry has launched the Digital India Awards?

options.en: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

questions.explanation_en: The Digital India Awards are instituted by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), with the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) running them. They honour exemplary digital initiatives by government bodies at all levels.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: How many scientists were awarded the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award, 2021 for Science and Technology?
questions.explanation_en: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology 2021 was announced by CSIR for 11 scientists across seven disciplines. It is India's top multidisciplinary science award for scientists below 45, named after CSIR's founding director.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: Which of the following terms is used for the rate at which commercial banks borrow money by selling their securities to the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation_en: The repo (repurchase) rate is the rate at which commercial banks borrow short-term funds from the RBI by selling government securities with an agreement to buy them back. The reverse repo rate is the opposite: the rate at which the RBI borrows from banks.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Delhi GK
questions.question_en: Under whose rule were the southern kingdoms annexed to the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation_en: The official key gives Mubarak Shah Khalji (1316–1320), during whose reign Devagiri (Yadava kingdom) was formally annexed to the Delhi Sultanate in 1318. Under Alauddin Khalji, southern kingdoms such as Devagiri, Warangal and Dwarasamudra had only been made to pay tribute, not annexed.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which of the following was set up by the Exim Bank and SIDBI in 2021 for identifying potential mid-sized and small companies as India's new champions in exports?
questions.explanation_en: The 'Ubharte Sitaare' Fund was set up by Exim Bank and SIDBI in 2021 to find and support mid-sized and small Indian companies that could become future export champions. It provides equity, debt and technical help to such firms.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: As of 2022, which of the following states has the highest number of assembly constituencies?
questions.explanation_en: Uttar Pradesh has the largest legislative assembly in India with 403 constituencies. Maharashtra has 288, Tamil Nadu 234 and Gujarat 182.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: What is the minimum age requirement, as prescribed by the Constitution, to become a member of a Panchayat?
questions.explanation_en: Under Article 243F, a person must be at least 21 years old to be chosen as a member of a Panchayat. This minimum age for Panchayat elections was introduced by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a vector borne disease?
questions.explanation_en: Malaria is a vector-borne disease: the Plasmodium parasite is spread by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. Diabetes and cancer are non-communicable diseases, and Covid-19 spreads directly through respiratory droplets.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Who among the following won the Golden Boot award during the 2022 FIFA World Cup awards?
questions.explanation_en: France's Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot at the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar with 8 goals, including a hat-trick in the final. Lionel Messi won the Golden Ball and Emiliano Martínez the Golden Glove.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: The final match of Ranji Trophy, 2022 was played between which two teams?
questions.explanation_en: The 2022 Ranji Trophy final was played between Madhya Pradesh and Mumbai in Bengaluru. Madhya Pradesh won by 6 wickets to lift its first Ranji Trophy title.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: With reference to the constitutional provisions regarding Rajya Sabha, which of the following statements is correct?

options.en: The Attorney General of India is the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The President of India is the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.explanation_en: Under Articles 64 and 89, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Deputy Chairman is elected by the members of the House.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which of the following man-made objects was the first one to cross the heliosphere of our solar system?
questions.explanation_en: NASA's Voyager 1, launched in 1977, was the first man-made object to cross the heliopause into interstellar space, in August 2012. Voyager 2 followed in 2018.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which of the following aims to create a competent civil service, rooted in Indian ethos, with a shared understanding of India's priorities, working in harmonisation for effective and efficient public service delivery?
questions.explanation_en: Mission Karmayogi (the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building), launched in 2020, aims to build a competent, citizen-centric civil service rooted in Indian ethos. It relies on online training through the iGOT Karmayogi platform.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who among the following is NOT amongst the Trinity of Carnatic music?
questions.explanation_en: The Trinity of Carnatic music is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, all 18th–19th century composers from Thiruvarur. Tenali Raman was a poet and wit in the court of Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya, not a Carnatic composer.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who among the following planned to launch a military expedition to bring the Khurasan region under Delhi Sultanate's submission?
questions.explanation_en: Muhammad bin Tughluq planned an expedition to conquer Khurasan (in Central Asia) and raised a large army for it, but the plan was dropped and the army disbanded. It is often counted among his 'ambitious projects', along with shifting the capital to Daulatabad and issuing token currency.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en:
The given pairs represent movements with the respective leaders. Which of these pairs is/are matched correctly?
i.Koya Rebellion - Tomma Dora
ii. Pabna Peasant Uprising - Bhagirath Manjhi
iii. Kharwar Uprising - Shambhunath Pal
questions.explanation_en: The Koya Rebellion (1879–80) in the Godavari hill tracts was led by Tomma Dora, so pair i is correct. The Kharwar uprising was led by Bhagirath Manjhi, and the Pabna peasant uprising (1873) by leaders like Ishan Chandra Roy, Shambhu Pal and Keshab Chandra Roy. Pairs ii and iii have their leaders swapped, so only i is matched correctly.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The temples at Khajuraho, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, were built during the reign of which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation_en: The Khajuraho group of temples (Madhya Pradesh) was built by the Chandela Rajputs, mainly between 950 and 1050 CE. They are famous for their Nagara-style architecture and intricate sculptures, and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Terms such as 'Pada Bheda', 'Chalis' and 'Bhramaris' are associated with the techniques of which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation_en: 'Pada Bheda' (foot movements), 'Chalis' (gaits) and 'Bhramaris' (turns) are technical elements of Odissi, the classical dance of Odisha. Odissi is known for its tribhangi (three-bend) posture and the chowk stance.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of the following Indian monuments is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation_en: The Charminar in Hyderabad (built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah) is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Red Fort Complex, Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb are all inscribed World Heritage Sites.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: In terms of power generation from renewable sources, which of the following sectors has the highest installed capacity in India as per the Annual Report, 2021-22 of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India?
questions.explanation_en: According to MNRE's Annual Report 2021-22, solar power had the largest installed renewable capacity in India (about 50 GW), ahead of wind (about 40 GW), bio-energy and small hydro. Solar overtook wind as the top renewable source around 2020.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: After Kerala, which of the following states or union territories has the highest scheduled caste sex ratio?
questions.explanation_en: As per Census 2011, Kerala had the highest sex ratio among Scheduled Castes (1057 females per 1000 males), followed by Puducherry (about 1056). Tamil Nadu came next at about 1007.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Who among the following gave the three laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation_en: Johannes Kepler gave the three laws of planetary motion (1609–1619): planets move in elliptical orbits (law of orbits), sweep equal areas in equal times (law of areas), and T² ∝ a³ (law of periods). Newton later explained them with his law of gravitation.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: In which of the following diseases does a parasite develop in the red blood cells (RBCs) of humans?
questions.explanation_en: In malaria, the Plasmodium parasite first multiplies in the liver and then invades and multiplies inside red blood cells. The bursting of these RBCs causes the periodic fever and chills. Dengue, Covid-19 and avian influenza are viral diseases.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Ajanta caves of Maharashtra are the cave monuments connected with which of the following religions?
questions.explanation_en: The Ajanta caves (Aurangabad district, Maharashtra) are Buddhist rock-cut caves, made from about the 2nd century BCE to the 6th century CE. They are famous for murals depicting Jataka tales and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who among the following Pala dynasty rulers was the founder of Vajrayana, Vikramashila and Somapura universities?
questions.explanation_en: Dharmapala (c. 770–810 CE), the Pala ruler, founded the Vikramashila Mahavihara (Bihar) and the Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur, Bangladesh), which became great centres of Vajrayana Buddhism. He was the son of Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The grants in aid by the Union government to certain States, charged to the Consolidated Fund of India, are described in Article ______ of the Constitution of India, 1949.
questions.explanation_en: Article 275 of the Constitution provides statutory grants-in-aid from the Union to states that need assistance, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. These grants are given on the recommendation of the Finance Commission, unlike the discretionary grants under Article 282.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of the following dance forms was also known as 'Dasi Attam' in ancient times?
questions.explanation_en: Bharatanatyam was earlier known as 'Dasi Attam' or 'Sadir', because it was performed by devadasis in the temples of Tamil Nadu. It was renamed and revived in the 20th century by E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Recently India test fired the surface-to-surface ballistic missile, Agni-5. What type of fuel engine does the missile have?
questions.explanation_en: Agni-5 is a three-stage, solid-fuel intercontinental-range ballistic missile developed by DRDO, with a range above 5,000 km. Solid fuel lets it be stored and launched quickly from a canister.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Ustad Zakir Hussain, the Indian music maestro, is known to play which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation_en: Ustad Zakir Hussain, son of Ustad Alla Rakha, was a world-renowned tabla maestro. He received the Padma Vibhushan (2023) and several Grammy Awards.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: The receipts which neither create any liability nor reduce the assets of the government are called ______.
questions.explanation_en: Revenue receipts are government receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce assets, for example tax revenue, and non-tax revenue such as fees, dividends and interest. Capital receipts, such as borrowings or disinvestment, either create a liability or reduce assets.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which state has recently, in November 2022, notified to implement the Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas (PESA) Act?
questions.explanation_en: Madhya Pradesh notified its PESA rules on 15 November 2022 (Janjatiya Gaurav Divas) to implement the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996. The Act gives gram sabhas in Fifth Schedule areas powers over local resources and governance.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: In December 2022, three women of Indian origin were selected as Australia's 'STEM Superstars'. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation_en: In December 2022, Science & Technology Australia named Dr. Indrani Mukherjee, Neelima Kadiyala and Dr. Ana Baburamani, all of Indian origin, among its 'Superstars of STEM'. Shruthi Bishnoi was not among them.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which state has major reserves of low-grade, brown coal called lignite, which is used for power generation?
questions.explanation_en: Tamil Nadu holds India's largest lignite (brown coal) reserves, mainly at Neyveli, where NLC India uses it for thermal power generation. Lignite is a low-grade coal with high moisture and low carbon content.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: As per the Handbook of Statistics on the Indian Economy, 2019-20, published by RBI, which Indian state has highest GDP?
questions.explanation_en: As per the RBI Handbook of Statistics on the Indian Economy 2019-20, Maharashtra had the highest Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) among Indian states, followed by Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh/Karnataka.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Where will the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships take place in India, in March 2023?
questions.explanation_en: The 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships were held at the K.D. Jadhav Indoor Hall in New Delhi in March 2023. India won four golds, through Nikhat Zareen, Lovlina Borgohain, Nitu Ghanghas and Saweety Boora.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of the following monuments is NOT located in Delhi?
questions.explanation_en: Bibi ka Maqbara is in Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Maharashtra. It was built by Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah in memory of his mother and is called the 'Taj of the Deccan'. The Qutub Minar, the Alai Minar and Balban's tomb are all in Mehrauli, Delhi.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who was the first Asian to be elected for membership in the British Parliament in 1892?
questions.explanation_en: Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 from Finsbury Central as a Liberal Party candidate, becoming the first Asian MP. He is known for the 'Drain Theory' of colonial economic exploitation.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: 'Bangar' and 'Khadar' are the sub-types of which of the following soils?
questions.explanation_en: Alluvial soil is divided into Bangar (older alluvium, found on higher ground, with kankar nodules) and Khadar (newer alluvium, found in the floodplains and more fertile). It is the most widespread soil in India, covering the northern plains.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Who is the first Indian woman to win a bronze medal in the Women's singles table tennis at the Asian Cup 2022?
questions.explanation_en: Manika Batra became the first Indian woman to win a medal (bronze) in women's singles at the ITTF-ATTU Asian Cup, in Bangkok in November 2022. She beat world No. 6 Hina Hayata of Japan in the bronze-medal match.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report, 2019, released in February 2022 by the Registrar General of India (RGI), which state had the highest infant mortality rate in 2019?
questions.explanation_en: As per the SRS Statistical Report 2019, Madhya Pradesh had the highest infant mortality rate (46 per 1,000 live births), and Kerala had the lowest. The national IMR in 2019 was 30.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which Indian badminton player secured a bronze medal in the men's singles at the BWF World Badminton Championships 2023?
questions.explanation_en: H.S. Prannoy won bronze in men's singles at the BWF World Championships 2023 in Copenhagen, losing the semi-final to Kunlavut Vitidsarn. It was his first World Championships medal.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: ISRO signed MoU with which of the following companies in January 2023 to support space-tech startups in India?
questions.explanation_en: In January 2023, ISRO signed an MoU with Microsoft to support space-tech startups in India, giving them access to Microsoft's tools, cloud platform (Azure) and mentorship. The move is part of opening up India's space sector to private players.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script?
questions.explanation_en: Article 343(1) says the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script, with the international form of Indian numerals. Part XVII (Articles 343–351) deals with official languages.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Narmada originates from which of the following places?
questions.explanation_en: The Narmada rises at Amarkantak on the Maikal range/Amarkantak plateau in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh. It flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and Satpuras into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: In which year did the Battle of Seringapatam, a war between Mysore and the British, take place?
questions.explanation_en: The Battle (Siege) of Seringapatam in 1799 was the decisive battle of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. Tipu Sultan was killed defending his capital, and the British restored the Wodeyars to a reduced Mysore.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Article 315 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?

options.en: Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States

questions.explanation_en: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union (UPSC) and a Public Service Commission for each state. The Finance Commission is under Article 280 and the Election Commission under Article 324.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Nalwari Fair is a cattle fair celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation_en: The Nalwari Fair is an annual cattle fair held in March at Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh, on the Luhnu ground. It features trade in cattle along with wrestling and cultural events.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides protection of life and personal liberty?
questions.explanation_en: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Courts have widened it to include rights such as privacy, livelihood and a clean environment.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who among the following composed the famous Tamil epic Silappadikaram?

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: At which Harappan site was a dockyard discovered, showing the civilisation's sea trade?
questions.explanation_en: Lothal in Gujarat (excavated by S. R. Rao) has a brick dockyard. It linked Harappan trade with West Asia.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under the patronage of which ruler?
questions.explanation_en: The Fourth Council met at Kundalvana in Kashmir under Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra. Buddhism split into Hinayana and Mahayana after it.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which of Ashoka's edicts describes the Kalinga War and his remorse over it?
questions.explanation_en: Major Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) and Ashoka's turn to Dhamma. It also mentions Greek kings to whom envoys were sent.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) praising Samudragupta was composed by:
questions.explanation_en: Harisena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti. It lists Samudragupta's conquests in north and south India.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The three Sangam assemblies of Tamil poets were held under the patronage of which dynasty?
questions.explanation_en: Tradition says the three Sangams were held at Madurai and nearby under Pandya kings. Sangam literature is the main source for early Tamil history.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which is the correct chronological order of the dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation_en: The Sultanate ran from the Mamluks (1206) to the Khaljis, Tughluqs, Sayyids and Lodis. It ended when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which Delhi Sultan introduced token currency, issuing bronze/copper coins to be valued at par with silver coins?
questions.explanation_en: Muhammad bin Tughluq issued token coins around 1329–30. The scheme failed because the coins were easily forged, and it was withdrawn.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which Sultan set up the Diwan-i-Khairat, a department to help the poor and arrange marriages of their daughters?
questions.explanation_en: Firoz Shah Tughluq created the Diwan-i-Khairat (charity) and a separate department of slaves. He is also known for canals and new towns such as Hisar.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: In the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated:
questions.explanation_en: In 1556 Akbar's army led by Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, the general of Adil Shah Sur. The victory secured Mughal rule in north India.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over:
questions.explanation_en: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza to mark his conquest of Gujarat (1573). It is the main gateway of the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: 'Amuktamalyada', a Telugu work on statecraft and devotion, was written by which Vijayanagar ruler?
questions.explanation_en: Krishnadeva Raya of the Tuluva dynasty wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu. His court had the eight poets known as the Ashtadiggajas.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at which fort?
questions.explanation_en: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad in June 1674. Raigad served as the Maratha capital after that.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by which Sikh Guru?
questions.explanation_en: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth and installed it at Harmandir Sahib. Guru Gobind Singh later declared the Granth the eternal Guru.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with which treaty between Tipu Sultan and the English in 1784?
questions.explanation_en: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) restored mutual conquests and ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War. The Treaty of Madras ended the first war and Seringapatam (1792) the third.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who commanded the East India Company's army in the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
questions.explanation_en: Major Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II at Buxar. The victory led to the grant of Diwani in 1765.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en:
Match the Governors-General with the measures of their time:
(a) Lord Cornwallis  (b) Lord William Bentinck  (c) Lord Dalhousie  (d) Lord Ripon
(i) Local self-government resolution  (ii) First railway line  (iii) Abolition of Sati  (iv) Permanent Settlement
questions.explanation_en: Cornwallis brought the Permanent Settlement (1793), Bentinck abolished Sati (1829), Dalhousie opened the first railway (1853) and Ripon passed the local self-government resolution (1882).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by which Act?
questions.explanation_en: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) gave Muslims separate electorates. Lord Minto was the Viceroy at the time.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
questions.explanation_en: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow (Awadh). Rani Lakshmibai led at Jhansi, Kunwar Singh in Bihar and Nana Saheb at Kanpur.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), which worked for the rights of lower castes, was founded by:
questions.explanation_en: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in 1873. He also wrote 'Gulamgiri' against caste oppression.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Santhal Rebellion (Hul) of 1855–56 was led by:
questions.explanation_en: Brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal Hul against zamindars, moneylenders and the British. The Santhal Parganas district was created after it.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was adopted by the Congress at which session, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation_en: The Lahore session of December 1929 adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal. 26 January 1930 was then observed as Independence Day.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Gandhiji undertook his first hunger strike in India during which movement?
questions.explanation_en: Gandhiji fasted during the Ahmedabad mill strike (1918) to support the workers' wage demand. Champaran was his first civil disobedience in India.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Kakori train action of 1925 was carried out by members of which organisation?
questions.explanation_en: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and others of the HRA looted the train at Kakori. In 1928 the HRA became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Who chaired the Boundary Commissions that drew the India–Pakistan border in 1947?
questions.explanation_en: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions. The 'Radcliffe Line' was made public on 17 August 1947.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Which was the first state formed on a linguistic basis, in 1953?
questions.explanation_en: Andhra State was created on 1 October 1953 after Potti Sriramulu died on fast. This led to the States Reorganisation Commission under Fazl Ali.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was a famous exponent of which classical dance?
questions.explanation_en: Kelucharan Mohapatra revived and popularised Odissi of Odisha. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Sattriya, recognised as a classical dance, originated in the monasteries of which state?
questions.explanation_en: Sattriya was introduced by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam. The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as classical in 2000.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en:
Match the folk dances with their states:
(a) Lavani  (b) Giddha  (c) Ghoomar  (d) Bihu
(i) Assam  (ii) Rajasthan  (iii) Punjab  (iv) Maharashtra
questions.explanation_en: Lavani is from Maharashtra, Giddha from Punjab, Ghoomar from Rajasthan and Bihu from Assam. Folk dances by state are a regular DSSSB topic.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a renowned player of which instrument?
questions.explanation_en: Amjad Ali Khan is a sarod maestro of the Senia Bangash gharana. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2001.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Sun Temple at Konark was built by Narasimhadeva I of which dynasty?
questions.explanation_en: Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty built Konark in the 13th century. It is shaped as the Sun god's chariot and is a UNESCO site.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The rock-cut Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was built under which dynasty?
questions.explanation_en: Rashtrakuta king Krishna I built the Kailasa temple, carved from a single rock. Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021, is located in:
questions.explanation_en: The Ramappa Temple at Palampet in Mulugu district, Telangana was built under the Kakatiyas. It was inscribed in 2021, the same year as Dholavira.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: The Hornbill Festival, held every December, is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation_en: The Hornbill Festival is held at Kisama near Kohima, Nagaland from 1 to 10 December. It showcases the culture of the Naga tribes.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: 'Bani Thani', often called the Indian Mona Lisa, belongs to which school of painting?
questions.explanation_en: Bani Thani was painted by Nihal Chand in the Kishangarh school of Rajasthan under Raja Sawant Singh. A postage stamp on it was issued in 1973.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian History, Art & Culture
questions.question_en: 'Mudrarakshasa', a Sanskrit play about Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power, was written by:
questions.explanation_en: Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa, which shows Chanakya's plans against the Nanda minister Rakshasa. Shudraka wrote Mrichchhakatika.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Who presided over the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946 as its temporary President?
questions.explanation_en: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was temporary President. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Objectives Resolution, which later became the basis of the Preamble, was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
questions.explanation_en: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted on 22 January 1947. Its ideals were reflected in the Preamble.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en:
Match the features of the Constitution with their sources:
(a) Judicial review  (b) Directive Principles  (c) Fundamental Duties  (d) Concurrent List
(i) Australia  (ii) USSR  (iii) Ireland  (iv) USA
questions.explanation_en: Judicial review came from the USA, DPSP from Ireland, Fundamental Duties from the former USSR and the Concurrent List from Australia.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which Schedule of the Constitution lists the 22 recognised languages?
questions.explanation_en: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages. The last four (Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali) were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form?
questions.explanation_en: Article 17 abolishes untouchability, and its practice is an offence punishable by law. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 gives effect to it.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous work is prohibited by:
questions.explanation_en: Article 24 is part of the Right against Exploitation. Article 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en:
Consider the statements:
I. Fundamental Rights are justiciable, while Directive Principles cannot be enforced by any court.
II. Directive Principles are contained in Part III of the Constitution.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation_en: Article 37 says DPSPs are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance. DPSPs are in Part IV; Part III contains the Fundamental Rights.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation_en: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties, added as Part IV-A (Article 51A). The Verma Committee (1999) later studied their implementation.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Who among the following does NOT take part in the election of the President of India?
questions.explanation_en: Under Article 54, only elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State and UT (Delhi, Puducherry) Assemblies vote. Nominated members do not.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Under which Article is the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation_en: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States. Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The 91st Amendment (2003) limits the size of the Union Council of Ministers, including the PM, to what share of the Lok Sabha's total strength?
questions.explanation_en: Article 75(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, caps the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha's total members. The same Amendment also tightened the anti-defection law.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Who decides whether a bill is a Money Bill?
questions.explanation_en: Under Article 110(3) the Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final. The Speaker endorses a certificate on it before it goes to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament cannot be called to resolve a deadlock on which bill?
questions.explanation_en: Article 368 requires each House to pass an Amendment Bill separately, so a joint sitting is not possible. A joint sitting is also not available for a Money Bill.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha submits a letter of resignation to:
questions.explanation_en: Under Article 94, the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker. The Deputy Speaker in turn resigns to the Speaker.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Under Article 85, the gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot be more than:
questions.explanation_en: Article 85 requires Parliament to meet at least once in six months. In practice there are three sessions: Budget, Monsoon and Winter.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Under which Article can Parliament create or abolish a State Legislative Council after the State Assembly passes a resolution?
questions.explanation_en: Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a Council if the Assembly passes a resolution by special majority. Such a law is not treated as an amendment under Article 368.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The 74th Amendment added which Schedule listing 18 subjects for municipalities?
questions.explanation_en: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects. The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule for panchayats.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Under the 73rd Amendment, what minimum share of seats in Panchayats is reserved for women?
questions.explanation_en: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts in Panchayats for women. Many states have raised this to 50%.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Finance Commission, which recommends sharing of central taxes with states, is set up under:
questions.explanation_en: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every five years or earlier. It recommends how tax proceeds are divided between the Union and the States.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which Article directs the Union to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language?
questions.explanation_en: Article 351 is the directive for development of Hindi. Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari the official language of the Union.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced the words 'internal disturbance' as a ground for National Emergency with:
questions.explanation_en: After the 1975 Emergency, the 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352. It also required the Cabinet's written advice for a proclamation.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The 103rd Amendment (2019) providing reservation for Economically Weaker Sections inserted which clauses?
questions.explanation_en: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) allow up to 10% EWS reservation in education and public jobs. The Supreme Court upheld it in Janhit Abhiyan (2022).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Election Commission of India is provided for under which Article?
questions.explanation_en: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission. It conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed under which Article?
questions.explanation_en: Article 148 provides for the CAG, appointed by the President. The CAG holds office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Which writ asks a person 'by what authority' he holds a public office?
questions.explanation_en: Quo Warranto stops a person from illegally holding a public office. Mandamus means 'we command' and Certiorari quashes orders of lower courts.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en:
Consider the statements:
I. A High Court can issue writs under Article 226 for enforcing Fundamental Rights and also for 'any other purpose'.
II. The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation_en: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and other legal rights, so it is wider than Article 32. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, while Article 226 is not.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: The collegium system of appointing judges originated from which case?
questions.explanation_en: The Second Judges Case (SC Advocates-on-Record Association, 1993) gave primacy to the CJI and senior judges. The 1998 case widened it to the CJI plus four senior judges.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Financial Emergency can be proclaimed by the President under which Article?
questions.explanation_en: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency, which has never been declared. Article 352 covers National Emergency and Article 356 President's Rule.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: Under Article 239AA, the Delhi Legislative Assembly cannot make laws on which of the following?
questions.explanation_en: Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment, keeps public order, police and land outside the Assembly's powers. These subjects stay with the Centre.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question_en: In which case did a nine-judge bench hold in 2017 that the right to privacy is a Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation_en: The Puttaswamy judgment held privacy to be part of Article 21 and Part III. Maneka Gandhi (1978) had earlier widened the meaning of Article 21.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: The longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwalik range, such as Dehra Dun, are known as:
questions.explanation_en: Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks are called Duns, e.g. Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun (NCERT).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which river rises in Rakas Tal near Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass?
questions.explanation_en: The Satluj originates in Rakas Tal near Mansarovar (called Langchen Khambab in Tibet) and enters India through Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which of the following dam–river pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation_en: Nagarjuna Sagar dam is on the Krishna river, not the Godavari. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent floods and shifting course?
questions.explanation_en: The Kosi often changes its course and floods north Bihar, so it is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'. The Damodar was called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which soil develops under high temperature and heavy rainfall due to intense leaching, and is well suited to cashew nut?
questions.explanation_en: Laterite soil forms where intense leaching removes lime and silica under heavy rain and high heat; with manure it suits cashew, tea and coffee (NCERT).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: The violent pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms of West Bengal in April–May are locally called:
questions.explanation_en: Kalbaisakhi ('calamity of the month of Baisakh') are pre-monsoon nor'westers in West Bengal and Assam. Mango showers occur in Kerala and Karnataka.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which state receives the bulk of its annual rainfall during October–November from the retreating (north-east) monsoon?
questions.explanation_en: The Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu stays relatively dry in the south-west monsoon and gets most of its rain in October–November from the retreating monsoon.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: The Khetri copper mines, among the oldest copper belts of India, are located in which state?
questions.explanation_en: The Khetri–Singhana belt in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan is a major copper belt; Balaghat (MP) and Singhbhum (Jharkhand) are others.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which state is the leading producer of bauxite, the ore of aluminium, in India?
questions.explanation_en: Odisha is India's largest bauxite producer; its Koraput and Kalahandi districts host the Panchpatmali and other deposits.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Geography & Census
questions.question_en: Which was the first biosphere reserve of India, established in 1986?
questions.explanation_en: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spread over Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was set up in 1986 as India's first biosphere reserve.

questions.question_en: Gross National Product (GNP) is equal to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) plus:

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: Primary deficit of the government is obtained by subtracting which item from the fiscal deficit?
questions.explanation_en: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments; it shows borrowing needed for expenses other than interest.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is compiled and released by:

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Indian Economy & Banking Basics
questions.question_en: Under the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), banks must keep a fixed share of their net demand and time liabilities as:

Cash, gold and approved securities with themselves

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: What is the SI unit of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation_en: From F = Gm₁m₂/r², G = Fr²/(m₁m₂), so its unit is N m² kg⁻². Its value is about 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which instrument is used to measure the relative humidity of air?
questions.explanation_en: A hygrometer measures humidity. A hydrometer measures the density of liquids and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation_en: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wider field of view, so it is used as a rear-view mirror.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: The twinkling of stars is mainly due to:
questions.explanation_en: Starlight is refracted by air layers of changing density, so the apparent position and brightness of a star keep changing, causing twinkling.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: The audible range of frequencies for the normal human ear is about:
questions.explanation_en: Humans hear roughly 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Sound below 20 Hz is infrasound and above 20 kHz is ultrasound.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: The heating element of an electric iron or heater is usually made of:
questions.explanation_en: Nichrome, an alloy of nickel and chromium, has high resistivity and a high melting point and does not oxidise easily when hot.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which of the following pairs of natural source and acid is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation_en: Ant sting contains methanoic (formic) acid; citric acid is found in lemon and orange. The other pairs are correct (NCERT Class 10).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: The chemical formula of washing soda is:
questions.explanation_en: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. NaHCO₃ is baking soda, CaOCl₂ is bleaching powder and CaSO₄·2H₂O is gypsum.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation_en: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals; copper is second and is used in wires because it is much cheaper.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Deficiency of Vitamin B1 (thiamine) causes which disease?
questions.explanation_en: Lack of thiamine causes beriberi. Scurvy is due to lack of Vitamin C, rickets to Vitamin D and pellagra to niacin (B3).

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation_en: Chickenpox is caused by the varicella-zoster virus. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are bacterial diseases.

questions.chapter: General Awareness — General Science (Class 10 level)
questions.question_en: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation_en: The liver is the largest gland; it secretes bile, which emulsifies fats in the small intestine.

questions.explanation_en: In July 2026 Mirabai Chanu won the women's 48 kg weightlifting gold with a Games-record 190 kg, India's first gold at Glasgow. Source: deccanherald.com

questions.explanation_en: R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women's Candidates 2026 in Cyprus (ended 16 April), the first Indian to do so. Source: chess.com

questions.explanation_en: The BWF World Championships were held in New Delhi on 17-23 August 2026, the first in India since 2009. Source: olympics.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which country won the Men's FIH Hockey World Cup 2026, beating Spain 1-0 in the final?
questions.explanation_en: Germany beat Spain 1-0 in Wavre on 30 August 2026 for their 4th Men's Hockey World Cup title; India finished 8th. Source: olympics.com

questions.explanation_en: On 8 May 2026 DRDO flight-tested an advanced Agni missile with MIRV capability from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha. Source: aninews.in

questions.explanation_en: On 4 September 2026 GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 (2,367 kg) in orbit from Sriharikota, ISRO's first success of 2026. Source: isro.gov.in

questions.explanation_en: In May 2026 DRDL Hyderabad ran an actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor for over 1,200 seconds for the hypersonic missile programme. Source: republicworld.com

questions.question_en: Under "Operation Urja Suraksha" (from March 2026), the Indian Navy escorts India-bound energy tankers through the:
questions.explanation_en: From 23 March 2026 the Indian Navy's "Operation Urja Suraksha" escorts India-bound energy tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Source: marineinsight.com

questions.explanation_en: The India AI Impact Summit in February 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, adopted the "New Delhi Declaration" on AI Impact. Source: newsonair.gov.in

questions.explanation_en: Union Budget 2026-27 (1 February 2026) set total expenditure at Rs 53,47,315 crore, a 7.7% rise. Source: prsindia.org

questions.explanation_en: Union Budget 2026-27, presented in February 2026, put capital expenditure at about Rs 12.2 lakh crore. Source: pib.gov.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: The 16th Finance Commission (Chair: Arvind Panagariya) kept the states' share of the divisible pool at:
questions.explanation_en: The 16th Finance Commission report, tabled on 1 February 2026 for 2026-27 to 2030-31, kept the states' share at 41%. Source: prsindia.org

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: MoSPI's new GDP series, released in February 2026, uses which base year?
questions.explanation_en: On 27 February 2026 MoSPI released a new GDP series with base year 2022-23, replacing 2011-12. Source: prsindia.org

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Before the October 2026 hike, at what level did the RBI keep the repo rate in its February-August 2026 meetings?
questions.explanation_en: The RBI MPC held the repo rate at 5.25% in February, April, June and August 2026, then raised it to 5.50% in October 2026. Source: prsindia.org

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: From 15 October 2026, UPI person-to-merchant payments above what amount attract a 0.4% MDR?
questions.explanation_en: From 15 October 2026 a 0.4% MDR (capped at Rs 300) applies to UPI merchant payments above Rs 2,000; smaller payments stay free. Source: prsindia.org

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: What was India's rank in the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2026?
questions.explanation_en: India ranked 38th of 139 in the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2026 (September-October 2026), 1st among lower-middle-income economies. Source: wipo.int

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: What was India's rank in the WEF Global Gender Gap Index 2026?
questions.explanation_en: In the WEF Global Gender Gap Index 2026 (September 2026), India stayed 131st of 145; Iceland was 1st. Source: yourstory.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Who was sworn in as the 23rd Lieutenant Governor of Delhi on 11 March 2026?
questions.explanation_en: Former diplomat Taranjit Singh Sandhu became Delhi's 23rd LG on 11 March 2026; Vinai Kumar Saxena moved to Ladakh as LG. Source: newsarenaindia.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Who was elected Mayor of Delhi on 29 April 2026?
questions.explanation_en: BJP's Pravesh Wahi (Rohini East) was elected Mayor of Delhi on 29 April 2026 with 156 votes; Monika Pant became Deputy Mayor. Source: newsonair.gov.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: What is the total size of the Delhi Budget 2026-27 presented by CM Rekha Gupta?
questions.explanation_en: On 24 March 2026 CM Rekha Gupta presented a Rs 1,03,700 crore Delhi Budget 2026-27, billed as a "Green Budget". Source: newsonair.gov.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026

questions.explanation_en: On 8 March 2026 PM Modi opened the Pink Line stretch from Majlis Park to Maujpur-Babarpur, completing India's first ring metro. Source: metrorailnews.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026

questions.explanation_en: As rolled out by DoE in February 2026, the Delhi School Education (Transparency in Fixation and Regulation of Fees) Act, 2025 requires a School Level Fee Regulation Committee in every private school. Source: tribuneindia.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: In February 2026 the Delhi Cabinet approved yearly help equal to the cost of how many LPG cylinders per ration-card family?
questions.explanation_en: On 4 February 2026 the Delhi Cabinet approved yearly assistance equal to two LPG cylinders for every ration-card family, paid around Holi and Diwali. Source: aninews.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which scheme in the Delhi Budget 2026-27 replaces the Ladli scheme?
questions.explanation_en: The Delhi Budget 2026-27 (March 2026) gave Rs 128 crore to "Lakhpati Bitiya", which replaces the Ladli scheme. Source: thefederal.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: The Delhi EV Policy 2026, notified on 1 July 2026, is valid until:
questions.explanation_en: The Delhi EV Policy 2026 was notified on 1 July 2026 and is valid to 31 March 2030, with road-tax and registration waivers for EVs. Source: dtnext.in

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: "Four Stars of Destiny" (February 2026) is the autobiography of which former Army Chief?
questions.explanation_en: "Four Stars of Destiny", the autobiography of former Army Chief Gen Manoj Mukund Naravane, came out on 12 February 2026. Source: currentaffairs.adda247.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: "Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles", released in August 2026, is the autobiography of:

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which book won the International Booker Prize 2026?
questions.explanation_en: In May 2026 "Taiwan Travelogue" by Yang Shuang-zi, translated by Lin King, won the International Booker, the first Mandarin-language winner. Source: drishtiias.com

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: Which country hosted World Environment Day 2026 (5 June)?
questions.explanation_en: World Environment Day on 5 June 2026 was hosted by Azerbaijan (Baku), with the theme "Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future." Source: worldenvironmentday.global

questions.chapter: General Awareness — Current Affairs — February to October 2026
questions.question_en: What was the theme of the 12th International Day of Yoga (21 June 2026)?

options.en: Yoga for One Earth One Health

questions.explanation_en: The 12th International Day of Yoga on 21 June 2026 had the theme "Yoga for Healthy Ageing". Source: pib.gov.in
